name: Shoal AI
description: Gives the other plugins in the family optional access to AI models (Anthropic Claude by default; OpenAI, Google and OpenAI-compatible services such as a local server), for decisions they can't make on their own. Nothing uses it until you allow it; spending limits apply overall and per provider, in your own currency.
overview: Optional, budget-controlled AI help for the Ingest and Subtitles plugins.

versions.changelog: 0.5.3-alpha: every button that calls the server shows progress while it works, and its outcome next to it.
0.5.2-alpha: the settings page always honours hidden elements.
0.5.1-alpha: the settings page uses the full width with centred buttons.

0.5.0-alpha: one budget page for every Shoal service: Subtitles' paid speech-to-text (Deepgram, OpenAI) is kept within the currency and limits set here; a tidier settings page; the call log pages 15 at a time with plain headlines, icons, relative times and details on expand.
0.4.0-alpha: a log of recent AI calls (caller, purpose, model, outcome, cost, duration; never what was sent) and the last error on the settings page.
0.3.0-alpha: paid calls and spending use the shared metering and spending store; unsupported currency codes read as USD; the currency list comes from the server.

0.2.0-alpha: text in any script reaches the model as written; exchange rates refresh when other plugins ask; clearer failure reasons for Ingest and Subtitles; replies that were billed but unusable are counted in spending; providers not available yet are shown as coming later.

First release. Claude through the official SDK (default Claude Opus 5.5), metered against overall and per-provider monthly limits in your currency; a Claude prepaid-credit countdown; an in-process entry point so Ingest and Subtitles can ask for help, each only when allowed on this page and only for its own purposes.

name: Shoal Ingest
description: Watches one or more drop folders. New media is identified from its release name and the server's own metadata providers, renamed to Jellyfin's naming standard (with provider IDs) and moved, with its subtitles, into the destination library for its kind. Release clutter is quarantined and purged after a retention period. Anything that can't be identified confidently waits on the plugin page for a decision.
overview: Watch drop folders and file new media into your libraries, correctly named.

versions.changelog: 0.13.0-alpha: move an automatically filed film or show to another compatible library from Recent activity; Delete now in quarantine can't clash with filing or leave a folder the purge skips; every action button shows progress while it works.

0.12.2-alpha: the review card says which title Ingest is using, with Replace existing copies up front and other shows under Wrong show; picking another show re-checks what's already on the server; the paused banner only shows when Ingest is actually paused.
0.12.1-alpha: the settings page uses the full width with centred buttons; summaries no longer add a full stop after a question mark.

0.12.0-alpha: tidier page (what the media is, one plain sentence, icon counts, relative times, details on expand, Show more); generic file names use the release folder; season-only names mean a series; the transcript now runs for unknown episodes; reviews of releases that are gone are removed.
0.11.0-alpha: undo a filed release from Recent activity; restore from quarantine and delete now; pause Ingest; new titles go to the library folder with the most free space.

0.10.0-alpha: Replace existing copies files the new copy where the replaced copy lives (same library and folder) unless another library is chosen in review; the review card says where; an empty folder left behind is removed.

0.9.0-alpha: state and search cache saved through the shared JSON store (flushed before replacing); the service is split into folder policy, start-up maintenance, quarantine and activity reporting, with no change in behaviour.
0.8.0-alpha: dry run per watch folder (on for new folders); a Waiting list with Process now; season and episode per video in review; theme-aware, more accessible settings page.

0.7.0-alpha: hard link or copy per watch folder, so torrents keep seeding (moved stays the default); Ingest remembers what it filed from there. Subtitle language tags in every ISO 639 language are recognised when filing, and unknown tags are kept rather than dropped.

0.6.0-alpha: releases needing a decision, failures, filings and quarantines also go to Jellyfin's Activity log, and Shoal Ingest is in the dashboard menu. Non-English metadata: English release names now match titles listed in the server's language. The library picked on a review card survives the refresh; missing watch folders are reported once; network (UNC) paths are accepted.

0.5.0-alpha: choose file by file in review. For a release with several files waiting, each file can replace its copies on the server, be quarantined (with its subtitles) instead of filed, or wait; the rest of the release is filed as usual. Replace existing copies and Quarantine release still act on the whole release.

0.4.0-alpha: Replace existing copies in review. A release held back because its episodes or films are already on the server (a better-quality copy, say) can replace them: the old copies and their subtitle files move to quarantine, restorable until it is purged, and the new files are filed in their place, all-or-nothing. Also: AI questions in any script fit its limit, the quarantine purge carries on past a stuck file, and non-ASCII digits in names no longer throw.

0.3.0-alpha: episodes whose names don't say which episode they are can be identified from a short transcript. With the Shoal Subtitles plugin (allowing Ingest to ask) and the Shoal AI plugin installed, two minutes of the video are transcribed on this server by default and the AI picks the listed episode whose synopsis fits, or none; anything else still waits for review.

0.2.1-alpha: episodes named by title only (typically specials, "S13SP2 A Special Title") are matched against that season's episode list from your metadata providers. When no title matches clearly, the Shoal AI plugin (if installed and allowed) may choose one of the listed episodes; anything else still waits for review.

0.2.0-alpha: optional AI tie-breaker. With the Shoal AI plugin installed and allowing Ingest, a close call between candidates Ingest already found is settled by the AI choosing one of them (or none), sending only file names, titles and years. Every choice is shown in Recent activity; anything else still waits for review.

0.1.8-alpha: review fixes. Libraries on a whole drive can be filed into; Jellyfin's metadata and transcode folders are protected; folder links and unreadable releases are handled. Quarantine never touches date folders Ingest didn't create, and "Quarantine release" is crash-safe and logged. Recovery only touches Ingest's own temporary files, a full disk after a move no longer splits a release, a hung network share can't stall filing, and choices on the review screen are checked against what the page showed.
0.1.7-alpha: a Quarantine section on the plugin page shows what is in quarantine (by date, per release, with file sizes) and the day each folder is deleted.

0.1.6-alpha: the plugin family is now called Shoal (this plugin shows as "Shoal Ingest"; settings and data are unchanged). Build hardening: pinned Jellyfin packages, locked restores, build-provenance attestation.

name: Shoal Subtitles
description: Finds subtitles for videos that are missing them (OpenSubtitles through Jellyfin, subtitles embedded in the file, other providers), scores the candidates, checks them against the actual audio and synchronises their timing. Speech-to-text runs locally by default (built-in Whisper), with optional cloud services. Every change is reversible.
overview: Find, check and synchronise subtitles so they match the audio.

versions.changelog: 0.16.3-alpha: every button that calls the server shows progress while it works, and its outcome next to it.
0.16.2-alpha: settings that should be hidden (billing key, download row, some buttons) no longer show when they don't apply.
0.16.1-alpha: the settings and results page uses the full width with centred buttons.

0.16.0-alpha: speech-to-text retries, falls back to a free local service, can be rerun with the chosen service, and flags only lasting problems; checks that can't run yet wait instead of guessing; tidier results page with Show more, icons, plain sentences and nerd stats on expand.

0.15.0-alpha: new videos are checked and searched about 10 minutes after they're added; choose which libraries the plugin works on; each library's subtitle languages are the default when the plugin's own setting is empty; Restore all originals before uninstalling.

0.14.0-alpha: whole-file discrepancy check for doubtful subtitles (off until switched on): missing lines, extra lines, names, numbers and negations compared with a full transcript and flagged for review with suggested fixes; full transcripts cached; optional confidence tuning.

0.13.0-alpha: last-resort subtitles generated from a full transcript when none can be found (off until switched on); added automatically and labelled generated, replaced when a real one is found; full transcripts have their own speech service; 20 a night within 4 hours by default.

0.12.0-alpha: the built-in speech-to-text downloads in the background with progress, and Test no longer waits for it; Test uses the page's unsaved spending limits; rewritten subtitles keep their group on Linux; provider errors quote the provider's own reply.

0.11.0-alpha: SubDL, Deepgram and speech-to-text calls go through the shared provider HTTP (capped, keys redacted, Retry-After kept); the find run stops on a provider limit or sign-in failure; one library walk and one run start; embedded tracks are checked when the only file beside the video is forced or picture-based.

0.10.0-alpha: built-in Whisper checks the system before downloading and gives up on stalled downloads; container- aware local service search; rewritten subtitles keep their file mode; nothing-found is not recorded when no provider answered; results saved in batches; settings that do nothing yet are marked coming later; page errors and accessibility.

0.9.0-alpha: languages are recognised from a built-in ISO 639 table, so the plugin works on servers without full language data. Subtitle languages accept codes or names (eng, fr, German); entries that aren't languages are noted in the log.

0.8.0-alpha: review in the results list: waiting items first, a filter and search, Decline, and Check again / Search again. Unclear results are checked again once speech-to-text changes; a new install waits until its settings are saved once. Subtitles waiting for review, added, or in folders that can't be written, and stopped searches, also go to Jellyfin's Activity log.

0.7.0-alpha: subtitle editor. Edit on a result opens the subtitle's lines: change text and times, add, delete and shift lines, find by text, and play any line's audio; Undo brings the original back. The built-in speech-to-text now installs under Jellyfin's data folder (on Windows it showed up as a broken plugin).

0.6.1-alpha: fixes. Subtitles in legacy encodings (Cyrillic, Central European, Greek, Turkish, Hebrew, Arabic, CJK) are written back in their own encoding instead of being garbled. An unreadable results file is never overwritten; folders that can't be written are detected before any download or check and not redone every night; one odd file can't stop the nightly run; ffmpeg found through PATH works; timings matched by meaning wait for review.

0.6.0-alpha: with the Shoal AI plugin (if installed and allowing Subtitles). Lines matched by meaning: when a subtitle's words don't match what is said (a translation, a paraphrase), the AI pairs them by meaning and the pairs must agree on one timing. Wording audit: lines whose meaning differs from what is said (names, numbers, a missing "not") are flagged with suggested wording that waits for review; subtitles checked earlier are audited a few per run. At most 20 AI checks per run.

0.5.0-alpha: short transcripts for Ingest (opt-in, "Let Ingest ask for short transcripts"). Ingest can ask for two minutes of a new video to tell which episode it is; uses the "Context for AI decisions" speech-to-text service (built-in by default, free and on this server), within the spending limits.

0.4.0-alpha: completes the first stage. SubDL as an extra subtitle source (with a free key; the right episode is taken from season packs). Opt-in checking of subtitle tracks inside video files (a corrected copy is added beside the video when a track is out of time). Deepgram credit balance on the settings page, with a guard that swaps an Admin key for a transcription-only key. A helper that finds a local speech-to-text service or shows how to run one.

0.3.0-alpha: paid speech-to-text (Deepgram, OpenAI) can be used by the nightly runs within your monthly limit, in your currency. Every call is priced from the providers' published prices, reserved against the limit and recorded; a call that would go over the limit, or whose cost can't be worked out, isn't made. The settings page shows this month's spending.

0.2.0-alpha: built-in speech-to-text. Once you allow it, whisper.cpp and a speech model are downloaded from this project's releases, checked against checksums built into the plugin, and run on the server's CPU. Also: undo is safe after another tool replaces a subtitle, large libraries are checked once each, downloads and huge files are capped, Apply/Undo errors are shown, downloads default to 10 a day and stop when the provider's allowance is used up, and forced-only tracks no longer count as having subtitles.

0.1.0-alpha, the first release: checks subtitle files beside films and episodes against the audio every day and fixes their timing (shifts and PAL frame-rate changes), first for free by matching line starts, then with a local speech-to-text service for the unclear cases; cleans adverts and bad timing; finds subtitles for videos that have none through Jellyfin's subtitle providers, adding one only if it fits the audio. Every change can be undone. The built-in speech-to-text and paid services in automatic runs are not in this release yet.
